principle_violations.reason: The 'Order' class has multiple responsibilities: managing order items and handling payment processing.
principle_violations.suggestion: Separate the payment processing responsibility into another class, such as a 'PaymentProcessor', and use it alongside the 'Order' class.

suggestion_code:
class PaymentProcessor:
    def pay(self, order, payment_type: str, security_code):
        if payment_type == "debit":
            print("Processing debit payment type")
            print(f"Verifying security code: {security_code}")
            order.status = "paid"
        elif payment_type == "credit":
            print("Processing credit payment type")
            print(f"Verifying security code: {security_code}")
            order.status = "paid"
        else:
            raise Exception(f"Unknown payment type: {payment_type}")

# Usage:
order = Order()
payment_processor = PaymentProcessor()
order.add_item("Keyboard", 1, 50)
order.add_item("SSD", 1, 150)
order.add_item("USB cable", 2, 5)
print(order.total_price())
payment_processor.pay(order, "debit", "0372846")

principle_violations.reason: The 'pay' method needs to be modified to support any new payment types, violating the open/closed principle.
principle_violations.suggestion: Define an interface or abstract class for different payment strategies and implement separate classes for each payment type to support extending without changing existing code.
